newsitem.title: THAILAND: S&P cuts IFCT counterparty ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts IFCT counterparty ratings.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Wednesday it cut the Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand's (IFCT) long-term counterparty credit rating to 'A-MINUS' from 'A' and its similar short-term rating to 'A-2' from 'A-1'.

"The downgrade reflects concerns surrounding the effect on asset quality flowing from Thailand's continued economic slowdown...(It) also considers the increased competitive environment facing IFCT over the medium term," S&P said in a statement received by Reuters.

IFCT is an industrial financing bank owned 30 percent by the government. S&P said the lower ratings took into account both IFCT's stand-alone financial profile and the likelihood of support from the Thai government, should IFCT experience financial stress.
IFCT's ratings outlook is negative, the rating agency said.

"IFCT has not been insulated from the deterioration in Thailand's financial system. The negative outlook reflects uncertainty the industry risks associated with Thailand's financial sector, which continue to increase."

But S&P said due to IFCT's relatively low exposure to the ailing property market and its strong investment appraisal standards, it is expected to maintain its asset quality at a level above that of commercial banks.
It said IFCT faced a structural funding limitation from its high dependence on wholesale borrowing that is viewed as a less stable funding source than retail deposits.
